officials.name: Kim Lund
officials.address: City Hall 210 Lottie Street Bellingham, WA 98225
officials.bio: Bellingham is an extraordinary place, and I show up each day to serve it with everything I have. I am committed to delivering actual results — expanding housing, strengthening services, and creating more opportunities for residents to thrive. This community’s best days are ahead of us, and I am honored to work alongside the remarkable people who are building them.

officials.name: Mark Ozias
officials.address: 223 E 4th Street Suite 4 Port Angeles, WA 98362
officials.bio: Commissioner Ozias is an experienced non-profit executive and former small business owner who has lived near Sequim since 2004. He has led and consulted for numerous organizations during his career, including serving as Director of the Sequim Food Bank immediately prior to being elected as Commissioner.

officials.name: Mike French
officials.address: 223 E 4th Street Suite 4 Port Angeles, WA 98362
officials.bio: Commissioner French is a former small business owner, with 15 years experience operating a restaurant in downtown Port Angeles. Born and raised in Clallam County, he received a Bachelor of Arts degree in Music from Central Washington University, and enjoys playing piano for various community performances. Prior to being elected as Commissioner, he served five years as an elected member of the Port Angeles City Council.

officials.name: Randy Johnson
officials.address: 223 E 4th Street Suite 4 Port Angeles, WA 98362
officials.bio: Commissioner Johnson is proud to have served in the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, rising to the rank of captain, and is a Vietnam veteran. He holds a Bachelor of Science degree from the University of the South and a Master of Business Administration degree from Harvard. Randy and his wife Carol have two children and two grandchildren, enjoying a rural lifestyle with 25 horses and two dogs.

officials.bio: Commissioner Cindy Carter, Republican, has been serving Grant County since 2006, currently in her fifth consecutive term working in the office. She represents District 3, which covers the area west of Moses Lake and south of Ephrata, and includes Quincy, George, Royal City and Mattawa.

officials.name: Kevin R. Burgess
officials.address: Room #206 35 C Street NW, Ephrata, WA 98823
officials.bio: Commissioner Kevin Burgess, Republican, has been serving Grant County since 2025, currently in his first term working in the office. He represents District 1, which covers the northern part of Grant County, east of Moses Lake, which includes Ephrata, Soap Lake, Wilson Creek, and Electric City.

officials.name: Rob Jones
officials.address: Room #206 35 C Street NW, Ephrata, WA 98823
officials.bio: Commissioner Rob Jones, Republican, has been serving Grant County since 2020, currently in his second term working in the office. He represents District 2, which consists of Moses Lake, Warden, and the area in between.

offices.name: Camano Office

officials.bio: Commissioner Janet St. Clair is from District No. 3, which encompasses the Whidbey Island area north of Oak Harbor and all of Camano Island. Her term of office is January 2019 to December 2026.

officials.name: Jill Johnson

offices.name: Camano Office
offices.address: 121 N East Camano Drive Camano Island, WA 98282

officials.bio: Commissioner Jill Johnson is from District No. 2, which encompasses all of the greater Oak Harbor area.

officials.name: Melanie Bacon
officials.bio: Melanie Bacon is currently Chair of the Board of County Commissioners and Commissioner of District No. 1, which encompasses all of Whidbey Island south of the greater Oak Harbor area.

officials.name: Brad Klippert
officials.bio: Councilmember Brad Klippert, who has called Kennewick home for 26 years, has previously served 14 years as a member of the Washington State House of Representatives. A retired U.S. Army veteran, he served more than 30 years in the military and 20 years as a helicopter pilot. He is currently a Benton County sheriff’s deputy and has served as a firefighter/paramedic. Klippert said he ran for city council to support smart, responsible growth while preserving what makes our community unique.

officials.name: Jim Millbauer
officials.bio: Mr. Millbauer has called Kennewick home since 1987 and was elected to the Kennewick City Council in 2019. He has been a pipefitter for 39 years and served as a Project Steward at Hanford, reflecting his values of serving others. His focus is on economic development, public safety, and building a better community through responsible growth.

officials.name: John Trumbo
officials.bio: Mr. Trumbo was elected to the council effective January 2014. His priorities include ensuring open and accountable government, growing industrial development, revitalizing the riverfront and downtown Kennewick, and addressing issues affecting the city's oldest and historic areas. As a retired journalist, he advocates public involvement in, and knowledge about, local government.

officials.name: Loren Anderson
officials.bio: Loren Anderson grew up in the Yakima Valley and moved to Kennewick in the summer of 2004 to start a dental practice. Loren and his wife, Danielle, have worked hard to create a successful practice, along with raising a large family. They have seven children and one daughter-in-law. In addition to work and family ventures, Loren has served in various capacities in his local congregation of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, and very much enjoys working especially with the younger generations. It is his faith that inspired Loren to run for city council, as a way to give back to his community and work for the improvement of Kennewick for all its citizens.

officials.name: Chuck Torelli
officials.bio: Charles (Chuck) Torelli has lived in Kennewick since 1985 and retired from Hanford in 2011 after a thirty-four-year career. He was appointed to the Kennewick City Council in 2019, then elected, and previously served on the Kennewick City Planning Commission. His priorities include economic development and managed long-term planning.

officials.name: Jason McShane
officials.bio: Jason McShane was appointed to Kennewick City Council in December 2023 and was re-elected in 2025, starting his new term in Ward 1, Position 1, in January 2026. McShane's top priorities for Kennewick include maintaining and improving fire and police coverage; enhancing the waterfront, including Columbia Park; enhancing parks and recreational opportunities; revitalizing downtown; supporting continued development of Vista Field and the Convention Center; and fostering economic growth through thoughtful planning and strong community partnerships.

officials.name: Paul Andrews
officials.address: 614 Division Street, MS-31 Port Orchard, WA 98366
officials.bio: As Kitsap County Auditor, Paul Andrews oversees elections, document recording, payroll, county finances, and licensing. He is President of the Washington State Association of County Auditors and serves on the Washington State Recording Standards Commission and the VoteWA Executive Steering Committee. Prior to his election, Paul spent over 25 years as an IT professional, focusing on modernization, transparency, and accessibility.

officials.hours: Monday - Friday 8:00 a.m. - 12:15 p.m. and 1:15 p.m. - 4:30 p.m. The office is closed for lunch from 12:15-1:15pm daily.

officials.name: Chad M. Enright
officials.address: 614 Division Street, MS-35 Port Orchard, WA 98366
officials.bio: Chad M. Enright took office as the 21st Kitsap County Prosecuting Attorney in January of 2019. He was raised in Poulsbo and attended North Kitsap High School, graduating from the University of Washington and Seattle University School of Law. He began his career with the Kitsap County Prosecutor's Office in 2008 as a felony trial attorney, focusing on special assault and mental health issues, and later served as Chief of the Felony and Juvenile Division.

officials.address: 614 Division Street, MS-37 Port Orchard, WA 98366

officials.name: Ross Nielson
officials.bio: Ross Nielson is a lifelong Washington resident and a strong member of the Lewis County Community, having served as a Boy Scout leader and volunteer in schools. With over 30 years of marriage and experience running a small business and as an Independent Fee Appraiser, he is dedicated to running the Assessor's Office efficiently, transparently, and ethically, prioritizing education, information, and respectful treatment for all.

officials.name: Scott Tinney
officials.address: Law & Justice Center on the 2nd floor, at 345 West Main Street, Chehalis, WA 98532-4802
officials.bio: The County Clerk, Scott Tinney is one of several independent, elected officials provided by the Washington State Constitution (Article IV, Sec 26), with specific and special duties assigned by statute, as well as local and state court rules. The position of County Clerk is best characterized as the administrative and financial officer of the Superior Court.

officials.name: Lindsey R. Pollock, DVM
officials.bio: Commissioner Lindsey Pollock, DVM, appreciates the opportunity to serve the residents of Lewis County, which she proudly calls her life-long home. Commissioner Pollock prioritizes how today’s decisions will have long-term impacts on the future of the county.

officials.name: Scott J. Brummer
officials.bio: Commissioner Scott Brummer says it’s a privilege to represent the people of East Lewis County. He has been a part of the Lewis County community for 30 years and says there is no better place to reside than in the State of Washington. Commissioner Brummer believes in retaining the core values of honesty, integrity, accountability and hard work at the center of county government.

officials.name: Sean D. Swope
officials.bio: Sean D. Swope is the Lewis County Commissioner for District 1, dedicated to public safety, employment opportunities, and economic growth. He advocates for accountability, responsible government expenditures, and supportive services for veterans, seniors, and low-income citizens. Commissioner Swope represents the northwest portion of Lewis County and holds a degree in ministry, with prior experience as a marketing specialist.

officials.name: Warren Mcleod
officials.bio: Warren McLeod was born and raised in the Boston area, working as an EMT for 14 years before moving to Las Vegas where he served as a Coroner Investigator for 11 years. In 2010, he was elected Coroner for Lewis County, beginning his first term in January 2011, a position that became full-time in 2015.

officials.name: Rob Snaza
officials.bio: Sheriff Robert R. Snaza was elected the 38th Sheriff of Lewis County in November 2014. He began his law enforcement career in 1990 and joined the Lewis County Sheriff’s Office in 1995, serving as a patrol deputy, Sergeant, and Undersheriff before his election.

officials.name: Arny Davis
officials.bio: Arny Davis was elected as Lewis County Treasurer in January of 2015, serving as the 28th treasurer since 1850. He previously served as Chief Deputy Treasurer and brings over 30 years of business management, finance, and accounting experience to the office. Arny chairs the County Finance Committee and oversees a staff of eight.

officials.name: Kamille Norton

offices.name: Marysville City Hall
offices.hours: Open Monday through Friday 8 a.m. - 4:30 p.m.

officials.bio: Kamille Norton served as City Council President from 2016 to 2024. Prior to serving on the Council, she served more than five years on both the city’s Civil Service Commission and Salary Commission. She holds a bachelor’s degree in Business Management.

officials.name: Kelly Richards
officials.bio: Kelly is a lifelong resident of Snohomish County, and has lived in Marysville since 2004. Prior to being elected to Council, Kelly served on the city’s Planning Commission (2011-2019) and is an active community volunteer. He works as a Paraprofessional at an elementary school in Marysville and previously was a real estate agent/broker.

officials.name: Mark A. James
officials.bio: Mark James and his wife, Renae, have been full-time local Marysville business owners since 2004 and are very active in this community. He is a veteran, a former President of the Marysville Sunrise Rotary club, and an active community volunteer. His desire is to leverage his experience to create a sustainable, attractive, and vibrant community.

officials.name: Peter Condyles
officials.bio: Peter Condyles is the president of the Marysville Historical Society and serves on the board of the League of Snohomish County Heritage Organizations. He previously served on several city and county committees related to growth management, community development, and housing. Condyles works as a project manager for Toyer Strategic Advisors and holds a bachelor's degree from Western Washington University.

officials.name: Stephen C. Muller
officials.bio: Stephen Muller is a lifelong resident of Marysville. Prior to his election to the City Council, he served 12 years on the Planning Commission, including 10 as Chair. As a community volunteer, he has served on the boards of the YMCA, Chamber of Commerce, Marysville Noon Rotary and the Food Bank, the Healthy Communities Leadership Committee, and overseen numerous school district bond and levy committees.

officials.name: Michael A. Stevens
officials.bio: Michael Stevens is a partner with Everett-based Dykeman Architects and previously served on the city Planning Commission. He holds degrees in Architecture from the University of Kentucky and the University of Pennsylvania, and has received Municipal Leadership Certifications. Stevens is an avid proponent of downtown revitalization and proactive city growth.

officials.name: Pat Tarzwell
officials.hours: M-F | Please check specific departments for office hours
officials.bio: With over 34 years of experience as the owner of AlphaTest, a successful local manufacturer of medical electronics, Commissioner Pat Tarzwell brings a wealth of knowledge, dedication, and leadership to his work in Mason County. His entrepreneurial journey—from dishwasher to business owner—has shaped his problem-solving abilities and provided him with the skills to approach challenges from a unique perspective. A passionate advocate for the growth and potential of Mason County, Pat is committed to fostering economic development through a focus on public safety.

officials.name: Alexis Mercedes Rinck
officials.bio: Councilmember Alexis Mercedes Rinck is honored to serve as a citywide Councilmember for Position 8, dedicated to empowering residents and ensuring access and opportunity for all. Her office supports policies that prioritize community safety, health, housing, and civil liberties.

officials.name: Bob Kettle
officials.district: District 7 (Downtown to Magnolia, including Queen Anne, Uptown, Westlake, Interbay, Eastlake, South Lake Union, and Belltown)
officials.bio: Councilmember Bob Kettle is honored to serve District 7, representing diverse neighborhoods including Downtown, Queen Anne, and Magnolia. He is dedicated to making Seattle a home for future generations, with priorities focused on public safety, public health, and homelessness. He pledges to represent constituents, prioritize oversight of city departments, and create evidence-based policy.

officials.name: Dan Strauss
officials.bio: Councilmember Dan Strauss is honored to represent Seattle's District 6, including Magnolia, Ballard, Phinney Ridge, Green Lake, Greenwood, and Fremont. He is committed to building a safe, affordable city full of opportunity and encourages residents to share their ideas for Seattle's future.

officials.name: Debora Juarez
officials.bio: It is a great honor to serve as your District 5 representative on the Seattle City Council.

officials.name: Dionne Foster
officials.bio: Welcome! It is a privilege to serve as your citywide Councilmember in Position #9 and represent diverse communities across Seattle. I believe local government is at its best when it helps people build fulfilling lives. As Chair of the Housing, Arts, and Civil Rights Committee, I'm committed to tackling the challenges that shape people's everyday lives.

officials.name: Eddie Lin
officials.district: District 2 (South Seattle, Yesler Terrace to Rainier Beach)
officials.bio: Welcome! It is an honor to serve as your District 2 representative on the Seattle City Council.

officials.name: Maritza Rivera
officials.bio: Hi, I'm Maritza Rivera. I represent Seattle's District 4, which includes the neighborhoods Bryant, Laurelhurst, Maple Leaf, Ravenna, Roosevelt, Sand Point, the U District, View Ridge, Wallingford, Wedgwood, and Windermere. I am grateful for and humbled by the privilege of representing the citizens and businesses of those communities. Public Safety is my number one priority.

officials.name: Rob Saka
officials.district: District 1 (West Seattle, South Park, Georgetown, and Pioneer Square)
officials.bio: I am honored to have been elected to represent District 1, a growing and dynamic area including West Seattle, Georgetown, South Park, Sodo, and Pioneer Square. Living in the Delridge neighborhood with my family, I've witnessed the district's progress and struggles. My legislative priorities focus on public safety, ending homelessness, affordable housing, and public infrastructure.

officials.name: Joy Hollingsworth
officials.bio: Hi, I'm Joy Hollingsworth, and I represent Seattle's District 3, which includes Eastlake, Montlake, Madison Park, Madison Valley, Capitol Hill, First Hill, Portage Bay, Leschi, Madrona and the Central District. I am a fourth-generation Seattleite, born and raised in the historic central district neighborhood. Our office is focused on the fundamental elements of essential government services that affect our day-to-day lives, and we are committed to serving all neighborhoods block by block focused on outcomes.

officials.name: Carolina Mejia
officials.bio: Carolina Mejia is a dedicated resident of Thurston County, serving her second term as Commissioner, which expires in 2028. She holds a Bachelor of Arts in Business Administration and previously worked as a Judicial Assistant with Thurston County Superior Court. Elected to the Board of County Commissioners in 2021, she is committed to volunteering and advocating for diverse communities.

officials.name: Emily Clouse
officials.bio: Emily is a lifelong resident of Thurston County and a proud alumna of North Thurston High School. Her journey of service began in the Army, where she served as a Military Intelligence Analyst. After her military service, Emily returned to Thurston County to manage two of her family's small businesses.

officials.name: Rachel Grant
officials.bio: A lifelong resident of Thurston and Mason counties, Rachel Grant brings over a decade of public service leadership to her role as Thurston County Commissioner. She has built her career on a strong foundation in behavioral health policy, finance, operations, and workforce investments, with a commitment to strengthening the systems that support those facing mental health and substance use challenges. Her extensive experience includes senior roles at the Health Care Authority and the Department of Social and Health Services.

officials.name: Tye Menser
officials.bio: Tye has lived in Thurston County for nearly two decades with his wife, an elementary school teacher, and two children. In 1993, Tye graduated with honors from Harvard College, with a degree in Government. In 1997, he graduated from law school at the University of California at Berkeley.

officials.name: Wayne Fournier
officials.bio: Wayne was born and raised in Tenino, Washington, graduating from Tenino High School in 1998 and later earning a Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy and Psychology from Washington State University in 2005. He has dedicated over 25 years to public service as a firefighter, serving as a mentor and instructor. Wayne previously served on the Tenino City Council and as Mayor of Tenino from 2015-2023 before being elected to the Thurston County Board of County Commissioners for District 4 in 2023.

officials.name: Barry Buchanan
officials.hours: Monday - Friday 8:30 a.m. - 4:30 p.m. Closed on holidays
officials.bio: Barry Buchanan is currently serving his fourth term on the Whatcom County Council. He was re-elected to the at-large (A) position beginning in January 2026. Councilmember Buchanan's term ends January 2030.

officials.name: Jon Scanlon
officials.hours: Monday - Friday 8:30 a.m. - 4:30 p.m. Closed on holidays
officials.bio: Jon Scanlon is serving his first term on the Whatcom County Council as the At-Large Position B representative, with his term expiring in January 2028. In 2025, he holds the position of Council Vice-Chairperson and chairs the Public Works & Health Committee, while also serving on other committees and representing the Council on various community boards.

officials.name: Ben Elenbaas
officials.hours: Monday - Friday 8:30 a.m. - 4:30 p.m. Closed on holidays
officials.bio: Ben Elenbaas is currently serving his second term on the Whatcom County Council, representing Council District 5. His current term began January 2024 and expires January 2028. In 2025, he chairs the Planning and Development Committee and is a member of the Public Works and Health Committee.

officials.name: Elizabeth Boyle
officials.hours: Monday - Friday 8:30 a.m. - 4:30 p.m. Closed on holidays
officials.bio: Elizabeth Boyle is currently serving her first term on the Whatcom County Council as the District 2 representative, with her term ending in January 2030. A former small business owner and organizational consultant, she focuses on public health issues like housing and the opioid crisis, and serves on the YWCA board. In 2026, she chairs the Public Works & Health Committee and is Vice-Chair of the Criminal Justice and Public Safety and Finance & Administrative Services Committees.

officials.name: Jessica Rienstra
officials.hours: Monday - Friday 8:30 a.m. - 4:30 p.m. Closed on holidays
officials.bio: Jessica Rienstra is currently serving her first term on the Whatcom County Council as representative of District 3, with her term ending in January 2030. In 2026, she chairs the Planning & Development Committee and is Vice-Chair of the Finance and Administrative Services and Climate Action and Natural Resources Committees. She also represents the County Council on several community boards and committees.

officials.name: Kaylee Galloway
officials.hours: Monday - Friday 8:30 a.m. - 4:30 p.m. Closed on holidays
officials.bio: Kaylee Galloway is serving her second term on the Whatcom County Council, representing District 1, with her term ending in January 2030. She brings a decade of experience across all levels of government, including the U.S. Senate and House, and volunteers on local committees like the Climate Impact Advisory Committee. With a Master's in Policy Studies and a Bachelor's in Politics, Philosophy, and Economics, her policy interests span economic development, climate change, housing, and public safety.

officials.name: Mark Stremler
officials.hours: Monday - Friday 8:30 a.m. - 4:30 p.m. Closed on holidays
officials.bio: Mark Stremler is currently serving his first term on the Whatcom County Council, representing Council District 4, from January 2024 to January 2028. In 2025, he is a member of the Public Works and Health Committee and the Climate Action and Natural Resources Committee, and represents the Council on several community boards.

officials.name: Julie Lawrence
officials.address: Yakima County Courthouse 128 N 2nd Street, Room 232 Yakima, WA 98901

officials.name: Amanda McKinney
officials.address: Yakima County Courthouse 128 N 2nd Street, Room 232 Yakima, WA 98901
officials.bio: Welcome and thank you for visiting our website. It is an honor to represent District 1 and work with Commissioners LaDon Linde and Kyle Curtis on behalf of everyone in our incredible Yakima County. My business background and community involvement have prepared me to deal with the important issues facing the County.

officials.name: Kyle Curtis
officials.address: Yakima County Courthouse 128 N 2nd Street, Room 232 Yakima, WA 98901
officials.bio: Kyle Curtis grew up in White Swan on the Yakama Indian Reservation and is a graduate of Eisenhower High School and the University of Washington. He returned to the Yakima Valley after working as a Financial Analyst, joining his family's diverse businesses. Currently, he serves as a Yakima County Commissioner, committed to accessibility, transparency, and collaboration.

officials.name: LaDon Linde
officials.address: Yakima County Courthouse 128 N 2nd Street, Room 232 Yakima, WA 98901
officials.bio: LaDon Linde has lived in the Yakima Valley since 1976, with a background in agriculture and healthcare. He is a fan of good government, emphasizing transparency, efficiency, and responsiveness to citizens. He has also volunteered extensively in community organizations.

officials.name: Reedy Berg
officials.bio: Reedy Berg is a lifelong resident of the Yakima Valley with a Bachelor's degree from Gonzaga University and a Master's in Education from Heritage University. He has worked as a teacher at Toppenish Middle School since 2016 and is committed to public safety, small business development, and creating a vibrant community for Yakima residents.

officials.name: Juliet Potrykus
officials.bio: Juliet Potrykus serves on the Yakima City Council representing District 4. She is a Yakima resident and mother of five with a background in public policy, education, housing, and community advocacy. Juliet brings experience working with legislative institutions, local courts, and community organizations, giving her a practical understanding of the systems that affect families, public safety, and economic stability. She is committed to the common good, safe streets, strong families, and affordability in Yakima.

officials.name: Patricia Byers
officials.bio: Patricia Byers moved to Yakima in 1978, working at the Yakima Family YMCA before earning a Masters of Psychology and working in behavioral health and private counseling until her retirement in 2015. A dedicated volunteer, she has served on various boards and commissions, including the City of Yakima Planning Commission, and is currently a licensed pastor. She is married to Harold and has two adult children, three grandsons, and one great granddaughter.

officials.name: Rick Glenn
officials.bio: Rick Glenn is a lifelong resident of the Yakima Valley, having raised his family in Yakima. He is a landlord, involved in several non-profit organizations, and an active church member. As a City Councilman, he aims to represent the entire city of Yakima and serve its citizens.

officials.name: Matt Brown
officials.bio: Matthew Brown was born in Phoenix, Arizona, and moved to Yakima in January 2006. He is married with two children and has been involved in his local community for years, with a passion for the Yakima Valley. As a small business owner, he aims to make Yakima a place where all small businesses can thrive.
